subject: Clarify: Reserved Pool Token Bandwidth SLO + Expansion Ops Plan
messages:
From: Lena Morris <lena.morris@averysys.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@averysys.com>, procurement@averysys.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — tokens/sec guarantees

Thanks Vanessa — we reviewed the renewal outline and the proposed Dedicated pool increase (3 -> 6 GPUs). Before procurement signs off we need explicit SLO language for token throughput per reserved pool and what happens during bursts. Two quick asks: (1) define tokens/sec guarantee and measurement window, (2) what credits or remediation apply if SLO is missed over a month.

Can your team send a short addendum we can attach to the renewal amendment? CC-ing Carlos (platform) and procurement.

-Lena

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Lena Morris <lena.morris@averysys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — tokens/sec guarantees

Thanks Lena — we can do that. I'm attaching a first-pass addendum (avery_slo_draft_v2.pdf) that spells out:

- Reserved pool nominal throughput: 1,200 tokens/sec per GPU (measured as sustained average over 5-minute windows)
- Pool-level guarantee: for a 6-GPU reserved pool the contracted baseline is 7,200 tokens/sec sustained (5-min avg)
- Burst allowance: short bursts of up to 2x baseline for up to 30s are supported and not counted as breach, provided system-level queueing does not exceed configured latency SLOs
- Measurement and reporting: Redwood metrics (per-route token counters + 5-min aggregation) are the source of truth; customers get daily token throughput reports and monthly SLO summary
- Remediation: SLA crediting for monthly breach = pro-rata percentage of monthly reserved capacity fees (examples and formulas in section 3)

This is intended as starter language — I want input from Karthik and Priyom on the operational and fallback mechanics (model fallbacks, cross-pool borrowing, and graceful degradation). Marissa, can you confirm whether procurement needs different phrasing for "burst" versus "sustained"?

Thanks — attaching pool_config_3GPU.xlsx with proposed physical layout and acceptance-test-plan.md.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0208

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — tokens/sec guarantees

Rolling up a few operational clarifications from infra:

1) Measurement details: we use per-worker token emit counters sampled at 1s and rolled to 5-min averages. The SLO window will be evaluated on 5-min aggregates; monthly breach = count of 5-min windows below contracted baseline weight-averaged by pool size.

2) Graceful degradation: when capacity pressure is detected we attempt prefix/KV cache reuse and model variant fallback (e.g., rwd-medium-quant -> rwd-small-quant) before shedding requests. If shedding occurs, we apply a defined drop policy prioritized by route.

3) Cross-pool borrowing: not automatic for Dedicated reserved pools unless customer opts in. For Avery we can propose a manual/automated borrowing clause: up to 15% of contracted tokens/sec can be borrowed from a linked spare pool for up to 2 hours, with chargeable burst increments. Borrowing is instrumented and appears on monthly usage exports.

4) Acceptance test: we need a 7-day soak with synthetic traffic to validate sustained baseline and burst behaviour. The acceptance-test-plan.md includes test vectors and pass criteria.

I'll convert these into plain-English language for the addendum and flag any items that require legal or product sign-off (notably the credit formula and borrowing clause).

-Karthik
Head of Infra Reliability (internal note: confirm how credits interplay with reserved-month refunds)

From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@averysys.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Lena Morris <lena.morris@averysys.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — tokens/sec guarantees

Appreciate the detailed draft. A couple clarifications from our side: (A) procurement wants the remediation formula to be deterministic — can you provide a sample calculation for a 30% breach in baseline hours? (B) we need to ensure the 7-day acceptance test includes a replay of representative queries (we'll share a trimmed dataset). Finally, on borrowing: Avery wants automatic borrowing enabled for the first 6 months of the renewal period as a mitigation while we ramp. Is that feasible?

-Carlos
Principal Platform Eng, Avery Systems

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@averysys.com>, Lena Morris <lena.morris@averysys.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — tokens/sec guarantees

Carlos — thanks. Quick answers and next steps:

- Deterministic credit formula: yes — we'll add a worked example. For contract language, Redwood proposes a monthly credit equal to (BreachFraction * ReservedPoolFee * 0.5). The multiplier (0.5) is customary to limit credits to a portion of reserved revenue; legal can adjust. Example will be in the updated addendum.
- Acceptance test: please share the trimmed replay set by 2027-05-04 so infra can schedule the soak. We'll run tests in a dedicated validation environment and share results within 48h after soak completion.
- Borrowing: we can enable "automatic borrowing" for the first six months as a paid buffer. It will be explicitly timeboxed in the addendum and subject to usage charges: borrowed capacity billed at 120% of the reserved token rate while in effect.

Action items:
1) Karthik to deliver refined ops wording and cross-pool mechanics by Mon 2027-04-26.
2) Vanessa to run the addendum by Redwood Legal for final phrasing and produce a DocuSign-ready version.
3) Avery to provide replay data and confirm acceptance window.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@averysys.com>, Lena Morris <lena.morris@averysys.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Finalizing addendum + DocuSign link

Team — attaching updated avery_slo_draft_v2.pdf (with Karthik's ops text and the worked credit example) and acceptance-test-plan.md. Highlights:

- Contracted baseline: 7,200 tokens/sec (6-GPU pool), evaluated on 5-min rolling averages.
- Monthly breach calculation: fraction of monthly 5-min windows weighted by pool size below baseline -> credit = BreachFraction * ReservedPoolFee * 0.5 (worked example included).
- Burst and borrowing: automatic borrowing enabled for first 6 months up to 15% of baseline; borrowed usage billed at 120% rate. Bursts of up to 2x baseline for <=30s not considered breach.
- Acceptance: 7-day soak with customer-provided replay; pass criteria = >= 95% of 5-min windows at or above baseline during test.
- Remediation: credits issued on next invoice unless parties agree to another arrangement.

Next steps for closing:
1) Avery sign-off on the attached PDF and send final replay by 2027-05-04.
2) I will route the DocuSign envelope once legal gives the green light. DocuSign draft: DocuSign: 3KJ8-AVY-SLO.

Please reply with any last redlines; if none, I'll ask Legal to issue the DocuSign this week.

— Vanessa
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
